newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Titan Cement puts off stock split.
newsitem.headline: Greek Titan Cement puts off stock split.

text.p: Greece's Titan Cement on Wednesday delayed a decision on whether to call a stock split because there was no quorum of holders of its preferred stock TTNm.AT.
An extraordinary shareholders meeting will be held on June 17 instead.
Titan Cement intends to capitalise reserves totalling 8.16 billion drachmas to raise stock par value from 1,620 drachmas to 2,400 before shares are split into two with a par value of 1,200 drachmas.
Shareholders approved the issue of a non-convertible bond worth 15 billion drachmas, denominated either in drachmas or foreign currency.
A forex-denominated bond would be issued at Libor plus 1.0 percent.
A drachma bond would be issued up to March 1999. It will be five-year paper, around 0.5 billion drachmas at Athibor plus 1.0 percent, paying a 0.25 percent issue fee.
Management told shareholders domestic sales volume in the first five months of 1997 is up 20 percent year-on-year.

Company president Andreas Kanellopoulos said half-year 1997 results should be 'much better' than in 1996 in the absence of market distortions stemming from loss-maker Halkis Cement. A smaller player in the domestic cement market, Halkis Cement followed an aggressive policy of marking down prices to capture market share. It has stopped its policy since coming under the umbrella of rival Heracles Cement, he said.
Management said it still eyed a collaboration with Heracles Cement through a participation in Halkis Cement.
Shareholders approved the distribution of a dividend per share of 460 drachmas for fiscal 1996, up from 320 drachmas a year earlier.
Both classes of Titan Cement's shares will trade ex-div on Thursday June 5.
On a consolidated basis, Titan Cement's 1996 pre-tax earnings rose 63.2 percent to 19.2 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 10.3 percent to 108.2 billion drachmas.
Parent company profit increased 50.2 percent to 15.7 billion drachmas with turnover advancing 15.9 percent to 74.1 billion drachmas.
Titan's common shares were off 1,285 drachmas to 27,465 on Tuesday on volume of 40,202 shares.
Preferred shares softened 1,010 drachmas to 22,610 with 18,350 shares changing hands. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
